plan: This is a second-price sealed-bid auction. In such auctions, the dominant strategy for a bidder is to bid their true private value. Bidding higher than the value risks a negative profit if the second-highest bid exceeds the value. Bidding lower than the value increases the chance of losing the item to another bidder when a profitable win was possible. Since my value is $20, bidding exactly $20 maximizes my expected profit regardless of the other bidders' strategies.

[ This is a second-price sealed-auction. In such an auction, the dominant strategy is to bid one's true value. Bidding higher than your value risks a negative profit (paying more than the item is worth). Bidding lower than your value increases the chance of losing the item when you could have won it profitably. Since the values are independent and there is no history to influence the strategy for a single round, I will bid exactly my value of $29. ]

Since this is a single-round game, and my value is $45, I want to bid slightly above what I expect the second-highest bid to be, but below my value to ensure a profit if I win. Without any history, I'll assume the other bidders will bid somewhat conservatively. I'll bid $38. This leaves room for them to bid higher, but still allows me to win and secure a profit if they bid below $45.
